messages.author: 27faf04482131169
messages.subject: can I analyze custom array?
parts:
Hi Henrik,

We have made custom SNP array for mouse (similar to SNP5). I have a
bunch of CEL files and a custom CDF. I really hope to utilize
aroma.affymetrix to conduct copy number analysis. Would you please
offer some hints? When I tried to use aroma, I was able to input data
but then got the following error:

+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
+++++
Error in list("process(acc)" = <environment>,
"process.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(acc)" = <environment>, :

[2008-02-21 09:25:57] Exception: Failed to retrieve genome information
for this chip type: MusCGDm520547_01
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Failed to retrieve genome information for this
chip type: ", chipType)
at throw("Failed to retrieve genome information for this chip type:
", chipType)
at getGenomeInformation.AffymetrixCdfFile(cdf)
at getGenomeInformation(cdf)
at getSubsetToAvg.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(this)
at getSubsetToAvg(this)
at getParameters.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(this)
at getParameters(this)
at process.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(acc)
at process(acc)
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
++++++

We were able to use apt-probeset-genotype to obtain raw intensities
(Plier). Is there a way to input these intensity data?

Thanks so much!

Jin

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] can I analyze custom array?
parts:
Hi Jin,

the answer to the question in the subject line is, sure. One of the
design goals with aroma.affymetrix is that is should work with custom
CDF with minimal setup.

On Thu, Feb 21, 2008 at 7:24 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> We have made custom SNP array for mouse (similar to SNP5). I have a
> bunch of CEL files and a custom CDF. I really hope to utilize
> aroma.affymetrix to conduct copy number analysis. Would you please
> offer some hints?

First of all, since you mentioning the similarity SNP5 chip type, I
want to make sure you understand the different between the "default"
and the "alternative" CDFs of the SNP chip type. For the latter, each
CN probe is in its own unit, whereas in the former, several CN probes
are bundled together in the same unit. You want your CDF to have one
CN probe per unit. This does not affect the SNP units, where you
have multiple probes per allele pair and multiple strands.

Second, make sure you work with a binary version of your CDF, because
an ASCII CDF simply be too slow to work with. You can use
convertCdf() in affxparser to convert an ASCII CDF to binary format.

So from you other message sent offline I know that you want to CN
analysis. With CEL files and a CDF file - but no other annotation
files - you can do all of the following:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("MusCGDm520547_01")
print(cdf)

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("MyDataSet", cdf=cdf)
print(cs)

acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs, subsetToAvg=NULL) # NOTE
print(acc)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)

plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300)
print(plm)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
print(ces)

More below.

> When I tried to use aroma, I was able to input data
> but then got the following error:
>
> +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
> +++++
> Error in list("process(acc)" = <environment>,
> "process.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(acc)" = <environment>, :
>
> [2008-02-21 09:25:57] Exception: Failed to retrieve genome information
> for this chip type: MusCGDm520547_01
> at throw(Exception(...))
> at throw.default("Failed to retrieve genome information for this
> chip type: ", chipType)
> at throw("Failed to retrieve genome information for this chip type:
> ", chipType)
> at getGenomeInformation.AffymetrixCdfFile(cdf)
> at getGenomeInformation(cdf)
> at getSubsetToAvg.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(this)
> at getSubsetToAvg(this)
> at getParameters.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(this)
> at getParameters(this)
> at process.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(acc)
> at process(acc)
> +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
> ++++++

The reason for this error is because by default
AllelicCrosstalkCalibration use argument subsetToAvg="-XY", which says
that it should fit the model parameters using all chromosomes but X
and Y. In order to infer what loci are on what chromosomes,
additional annotation data beyond the CDF is required, namely genomic
locations for each unit (loci). In my example above, I circumvent
this by saying all units can be used to fit the model, which is
suboptimal. Instead...

You will need to setup a so called Unit Genome Position (UGP)
annotation file which contains a (unit, chromosome, position) map
specific to given CDF. If you have a NetAffx containing this
information, you can follow the instructions on how it was done for
the GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/genomewidesnp-6---miscellaneous

If you don't have a NetAffx-like data file, you can still allocate an
empty UGP file, e.g.

ugp <- AromaUgpFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="JP20080221");
print(ugp)

and populate the UGP map yourself, e.g.

# Set the chromosomes for the first seven units
ugp[,1] <- c(1,1,2,2,3,4,5)

# ...and their physical positions
ugp[,2] <- c(13410,43031,10322,10323,34303,12304,40335)

Note that the rows in the UGP table should map one-to-one to the units
in the CDF, e.g.

unitName <- "SNP_A-123231"
unit <- indexOf(cdf, unitName)
stopifnot(getUnitNames(cdf, unit), unitName)

...and the genome position for this unit should be:

print(ugp[unit,])

You will also need the UGP for doing the segmentation later on.

Similarly, if you want to do the fragment-length normalization (as
suggested in the vignette), also need to create a Unit Fragment Length
(UFL) annotation file for your custom CDF. I'll leave that for now,
but the idea is very similar, cf.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/building-ufl-file-for-genomewidesnp-6

>
> We were able to use apt-probeset-genotype to obtain raw intensities
> (Plier). Is there a way to input these intensity data?

There are some notes on this at:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/import-from-affymetrix-power-tools-apt

Yet again, you will still need UGP annotation data in order to proceed
to the segmentation step.

Finally, as a group member, you're welcome to write up your own notes
in a Subpage to 'Documentation on chip types' (under "Pages") for your
custom chip type/CDF. There you can also show how you create the UGP
etc.

Hope this helps you get started.

/Henrik

PS. Since this message already contains many different topics, for
future messages, please use a separate thread/subject line for each
topic. DS.

>
> Thanks so much!
>
> Jin
>
>
> >
>

second difference from the commercial SNP 5 chip is that we don't have

and are binary.

From your output I can only conclude that your custom CDF does not
conform to the same "standards" as the other Affymetrix SNP chips,
e.g. it fails to identify the SNP units in the first place.

Could you post the CDF (preferably gzip/zip:ped!) somewhere so I can
have a look at it so I can update AllelicCrosstalkCalibration to deal
with as well. If you also have a CEL file (gzipped) that I can play
with, that would certainly help.

You can forward the URLs in a private message if you want to.

/Henrik

messages.author: 27faf04482131169
messages.subject: Re: can I analyze custom array?
parts:
Hi Henrik,

(1) I only have snp probesets on my custom array, should I use
RmaCnPlm()?
(2) is there a way to output the chip effect (ces) or allocate them in
a matrix? We want to implement a different way of specifiying
reference and then run R/DNAcopy for segmentation.
(3) the chromosome explorer is only for human array (hg18), correct?

command that I used:
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs, subsetToAvg=NULL) # NOTE

print(acc)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)

plm <- RmaCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
+300)

print(plm)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
print(ces)

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: can I analyze custom array?
parts:
On Tue, Mar 4, 2008 at 11:24 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> (1) I only have snp probesets on my custom array, should I use
> RmaCnPlm()?

Sure. There is also AvgCnPlm() that can be used if the probes are
technical replicates (as in GWS5 and GWS6). The latter is a
single-array summarization method and our current results indicate
that the RmaCnPlm() is slightly better; we don't know the exact reason
for, maybe it is because the estimates are more robust.

> (2) is there a way to output the chip effect (ces) or allocate them in
> a matrix? We want to implement a different way of specifiying
> reference and then run R/DNAcopy for segmentation.

See the Vignette 'Calculating raw total copy numbers manually'
illustrating how to use extractMatrix(). In the latest version there
is also extractDataFrame(), e.g.

data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=1000:1100, addNames=TRUE)
print(data[1:5,1:7])
## unitName groupName unit group cell NA06985 NA06991
## 1 SNP_A-2001405 A 1000 1 1378 7110.703 5463.868
## 2 SNP_A-4214079 C 1001 1 1380 12249.886 9743.836
## 3 SNP_A-2001454 C 1002 1 1382 2957.766 3974.954
## 4 SNP_A-2001478 C 1003 1 1384 4597.873 6187.850
## 5 SNP_A-2001480 C 1004 1 1386 4605.493 5032.741
> (3) the chromosome explorer is only for human array (hg18), correct?

I'm not sure what part of the ChromosomeExplorer you refer to. If you
ignore the cytobands which are the ones specified by the GLAD package
(don't know what version of the HG that uses), the ChromosomeExplorer
(which in turn utilizes the segmentation model) uses whatever UGP
annotation data you have.

>
> command that I used:
>
>
> acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs, subsetToAvg=NULL) # NOTE
> print(acc)
>
> csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
>
> plm <- RmaCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
>
> +300)
> print(plm)
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
>
> ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
> print(ces)

Seems alright to me.

Henrik

>
>
>
> >
